newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's Abiola not to be in court to name lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Abiola not to be in court to name lawyer.

text.p: A Nigerian judge ruled on Tuesday that detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola should not be present in court to name the lawyer to represent him at his treason trial.

Justice Umaru Kalgo of the Federal Court of Appeal sitting in the Nigerian capital dismissed a lower court's order that Abiola must be produced in court by the military government to name which of two lawyers should represent him.
In April last year in Abuja, the lower Federal High Court ordered that Abiola be brought to court to name his treason trial lawyer. The government appealed against the ruling.

Kalgo said: "The order of the lower court is improper as there is no provision in law or our constitution entitling a judge to consult a respondent (Abiola) in decisions to choose a lawyer or to resolve issue of representation for him."
Two of Nigeria's top lawyers are bickering over who will take the case. Neither lawyer was in court on Tuesday.
Africa's most populous nation has been in political crisis since a previous army government annulled a 1993 presidential poll which Abiola is widely believed to have won.
The millionaire businessman has been detained since June 1994 when he was arrested and charged with treason for proclaiming himself president in defiance of military ruler General Sani Abacha.
Kalgo said Abiola needed no assistance from the court to choose his lawyer, adding: "The court should not be seen to have any hand in Abiola's decisions to ensure unbiased and fair trial."
No lawyer has been allowed to see Abiola since October 1994.
Nigeria has been shunned by Western countries for human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
